11: ## Project Overview
12: 
13: **Northstar** is a tvOS 26 SwiftUI application that provides an Xbox cloud gaming client (xCloud / Game Pass) for Apple TV. It is the single app target in this monorepo. The repo also contains seven Swift Package Manager packages that the app target consumes.
14: 
15: - **App target:** `Apps/Northstar/` (product name: Northstar, brand: NORTHSTAR)
16: - **Packages:** `Packages/` — DiagnosticsKit, NorthstarCore, NorthstarModels, InputBridge, StreamingCore, VideoRenderingKit, XCloudAPI
17: - **Third-party:** `ThirdParty/WebRTC/WebRTC.xcframework` — pre-built binary, tvOS arm64 + simulator
18: - **Tools:** `Tools/webrtc-build/` — build scripts and tvOS-specific patches for the WebRTC source
19: 
20: The app streams cloud games over WebRTC. The UI layer is SwiftUI throughout. The rendering layer uses Metal. Audio is managed via AVAudioSession with tvOS-specific patches applied to the WebRTC framework.

152: ## Architecture
153: 
154: ### Boot sequence
155: 
156: `NorthstarApp` (SwiftUI `@main`) creates one `AppCoordinator` from `NorthstarCore` and injects all of its controllers as typed environment objects:
157: 
158: ```
159: NorthstarApp
160:   └── AppCoordinator (NorthstarCore, @MainActor, ObservableObject)
161:         ├── sessionController
162:         ├── libraryController
163:         ├── profileController
164:         ├── consoleController
165:         ├── streamController
166:         ├── shellBootstrapController
167:         ├── achievementsController
168:         ├── inputController
169:         ├── previewExportController
170:         └── settingsStore
171: ```
172: 
173: `RootView` reads auth state from `AppCoordinator` and routes to: `AuthView` → `DeviceCodeView` → authenticated shell.
174: 
175: ### Shell layers
176: 
177: `AuthenticatedShellView` (in `Shell/`) is the container for the authenticated experience. It wraps `CloudLibraryView` as the primary content. `GamePassShellView`/`MainTabView` provide ambient background and top-chrome overlay.
178: 
179: ### CloudLibrary feature (largest feature slice)
180: 
181: ```
182: CloudLibraryView              ← coordinator-connected entry
183:   └── CloudLibraryShellHost   ← layout + action routing owner
184:         ├── CloudLibraryShellView       ← side rail + content host
185:         ├── CloudLibraryContentRouteHost← routes to browse/utility/detail
186:         ├── CloudLibraryBrowseRouteHost ← home/library/search/consoles
187:         └── CloudLibraryUtilityRouteHost← profile/settings overlays
188: ```
189: 
190: **State objects (all @MainActor, @Observable):**
191: - `CloudLibraryViewModel` — source of truth for all library data projections
192: - `CloudLibrarySceneModel` — scene-level derived state (routes, hero bg, status)
193: - `CloudLibraryPresentationStore` — presentation projection cache
194: - `CloudLibraryRouteState` — current browse/utility/detail routes
195: - `CloudLibraryFocusState` — focus request tokens and settled tile state
196: - `CloudLibraryLoadState` — loading/error/success envelope
197: 
198: **Data shaping (`Data/CloudLibrary/`):** All transformation from raw library models to view state is side-effect-free and has no async work. These functions are pure and testable without mocks.
199: 
200: ### Action routing
201: 
202: `CloudLibraryShellHost` owns the three routed action bags directly through its `browseActions`, `detailActions`, and `utilityActions` computed properties. The former `CloudLibraryActionFactory` passthrough seam is already dissolved.
203: 
204: `CloudLibraryBrowseRouteActions`, `CloudLibraryDetailRouteActions`, and `CloudLibraryUtilityRouteActions` remain the correct boundary types. Keep closures in these routed action structs explicitly `@MainActor` when they are invoked from `@MainActor` UI code.
205: 
206: ### Streaming feature
207: 
208: ```
209: StreamView
210:   └── StreamModalControllerHost
211:         ├── StreamOverlay (overlay controls + diagnostics)
212:         └── RenderSurfaceCoordinator
213:               └── RendererAttachmentCoordinator (@MainActor)
214:                     ├── MetalVideoRenderer (Integration/WebRTC/)
215:                     └── SampleBufferDisplayRenderer (series of extensions)
216: ```
217: 
218: `RendererAttachmentCoordinator` is `@MainActor` and manages renderer selection, lifecycle, and fallback. The UIKit/probe support types now live under `Features/Streaming/Rendering/UIKitAdapters/`, leaving the coordinator focused on policy and attachment work.
219: 
220: ### Package roles
221: 
222: | Package | Role | Key constraint |
223: |---------|------|----------------|
224: | `NorthstarCore` | App lifecycle, auth, controllers, hydration | Owns `AppCoordinator`. No UI. |
225: | `NorthstarModels` | Shared model types | No dependencies on other packages |
226: | `XCloudAPI` | Network layer — xCloud API, auth, catalog | No UI |
227: | `StreamingCore` | WebRTC session, SDP/ICE, channels | No Metal, no UIKit |
228: | `VideoRenderingKit` | Upscale strategy resolution | No UIKit, no Metal directly |
229: | `InputBridge` | Gamepad input, input queue | No UI |
230: | `DiagnosticsKit` | Metrics pipeline, logging, telemetry | No UI |
231: 
232: Packages do not depend on the app target. The app target depends on packages. Packages may depend on each other only along the data-flow direction (NorthstarCore → XCloudAPI, StreamingCore; not the reverse).
233: 
234: ### WebRTC integration
235: 
236: `Integration/WebRTC/` is the boundary layer between the WebRTC binary framework and the rest of the app. Everything in this directory is conditionally compiled with `#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE`. Outside this directory, the app uses protocol abstractions from `StreamingCore` and `NorthstarCore`.
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ## Concurrency Model (Layered Actor Strategy)
241: 
242: This project uses a **layered actor strategy**. "Everything is MainActor" is not the model. "Nonisolated by default" is not the model.
243: 
244: **Layer 1 — UI and navigation (@MainActor)**
245: All SwiftUI views, all view models (`CloudLibraryViewModel`, `CloudLibrarySceneModel`, etc.), all focus/route state. These are `@MainActor` and must remain so. Do not add background threading to UI state without explicit justification.
246: 
247: **Layer 2 — Service and cache (isolated actors)**
248: `RemoteImagePipeline` in `Shared/Theme/RemoteImagePipeline.swift` is a correct example: an `actor` that owns a mutable cache and an in-flight deduplication dictionary. New shared, mutable, cross-cutting state belongs in a named actor, not in a `nonisolated` class protected by `NSLock` unless benchmark evidence requires it.
249: 
250: **Layer 3 — Rendering and compute (explicit concurrency)**
251: Metal rendering runs off the main thread via `MTKViewDelegate` callbacks. Heavy async work (image decoding, frame processing) must use `@concurrent` when called from `@MainActor` context. Do not mark rendering code `@MainActor` unless it is purely UI.
252: 
253: **Cross-boundary closures:** All action closures that originate in `@MainActor` view code must be annotated `@MainActor (...) -> Void` to make isolation explicit. Do not use untyped `@escaping` closures at `@MainActor` boundaries.
254: 
255: ---

257: ## Testing Strategy
258: 
259: ### Test targets
260: 
261: | Target | Framework | Scope |
262: |--------|-----------|-------|
263: | `NorthstarTests` | XCTest (migrating to Swift Testing) | Unit tests for state, routing, data shaping, focus, streaming |
264: | `NorthstarUITests` | XCTest (XCUI) | Shell checkpoint captures |
265: | `NorthstarPerformanceTests` | XCTest | Launch, route switch, post-stream freshness |
266: | `NorthstarPerformanceUITests` | XCTest | Performance UI scenarios |
267: | Per-package `Tests/` | Swift Testing (new) / XCTest (existing) | Package-level unit tests |
268: 
269: ### Rules
270: 
271: 1. **Swift Testing** (`import Testing`) is the target framework for new pure-Swift unit tests. Migrate existing XCTest unit tests incrementally when touching a file.
272: 2. **XCTest + XCUI** must remain for all UI automation. Swift Testing does not replace XCUI.
273: 3. **No mocking the WebRTC layer** in unit tests. Use `#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE` guards and test against the mock/stub path.
274: 4. **Data shaping tests** (`Data/CloudLibrary/`) are pure function tests — no async, no mocks needed.
275: 5. **Performance tests** use the dedicated `Northstar-Perf` scheme.
276: 
277: ### CI workflows (`.github/workflows/`)

279: | Workflow | What it validates |
280: |----------|------------------|
281: | `ci-app-build-and-smoke.yml` | Full app build + `AppSmokeTests` |
282: | `ci-packages.yml` | All SPM package tests |
283: | `ci-pr-fast-guards.yml` | Fast guard checks on PRs |
284: | `ci-shell-ui.yml` | Shell UI tests |
285: | `ci-shell-visual-regression.yml` | Visual regression checkpoints |
286: | `ci-runtime-safety.yml` | Runtime safety checks |
287: | `ci-release-and-validation.yml` | Release build + `Northstar-Validation` scheme |
288: | `ci-hardware-device.yml` | Hardware device integration |

292: ## Execution Agreements
293: 
294: These are the rules all agents in this repo must follow. They are not optional.
295: 
296: ### Structural agreements
297: 
298: 1. **Do not create new files without justification.** The project already has a large source surface. New files must represent a genuinely new seam, not a preference for smaller files.
299: 2. **Do not split files unless the split resolves a mixed-responsibility root.** Over-splitting is already an identified problem. Creating additional micro-shards makes it worse.
300: 3. **Do not merge files unless the merge removes an artificial seam.** Merge only what is identified in the Floor/Execution contracts or a newly approved cleanup wave.
301: 4. **Reference images must live in one canonical location.** `Apps/Northstar/Tools/shell-visual-regression/reference/` is the canonical location. Do not create a second reference image directory.
302: 5. **Remove `.DS_Store` files** if encountered. Do not commit them.
303: 
304: ### Code agreements
305: 
306: 6. **Strict concurrency is always on.** Every new type must declare its isolation. If you add a class, decide: `@MainActor`, actor, or nonisolated with explicit Sendable conformance.
307: 7. **`#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE` guards are mandatory** in `Integration/WebRTC/`. Do not remove them or add WebRTC symbol references outside this directory.
308: 8. **Do not add `@unchecked Sendable`** without a comment explaining why the type cannot conform normally and what invariant makes it safe.
309: 9. **Action closures at UI boundaries** must be annotated `@MainActor` when the closure will be called from `@MainActor` context.
310: 10. **`Task { @MainActor in ... }` is a smell at call sites** in view code. If you are wrapping a UI update in a detached Task inside a view, reconsider whether the caller should be async or whether the state object needs an actor boundary.
311: 
312: ### Testing agreements
313: 
314: 11. **New unit tests for pure-Swift logic** go in Swift Testing (`import Testing`).
315: 12. **New unit tests for state machines** go under `NorthstarTests/` with a name matching the type under test (e.g., `CloudLibraryRouteStateTests.swift` for `CloudLibraryRouteState`).
316: 13. **Do not add XCTest unit tests to targets that are migrating to Swift Testing.** Only add Swift Testing tests.
317: 14. **Do not change the CI workflow files** without understanding what guards they enforce. If a workflow must change, document the reason in a comment in the file.
318: 
319: ### Package agreements
320: 
321: 15. **Packages do not import the app target.** The dependency direction is always app → package, never package → app.
322: 16. **`NorthstarModels` has no package dependencies.** It must remain the leaf-level shared model package.
323: 17. **New model types** that are shared across packages go in `NorthstarModels`, not in the app target.
324: 18. **New network types** go in `XCloudAPI`, not in the app target.
325: 19. **New diagnostic/metrics types** go in `DiagnosticsKit`, not in the app target.

## Architecture

### Boot sequence

`NorthstarApp` (SwiftUI `@main`) creates one `AppCoordinator` from `NorthstarCore` and injects all of its controllers as typed environment objects:

```
NorthstarApp
  └── AppCoordinator (NorthstarCore, @MainActor, ObservableObject)
        ├── sessionController
        ├── libraryController
        ├── profileController
        ├── consoleController
        ├── streamController
        ├── shellBootstrapController
        ├── achievementsController
        ├── inputController
        ├── previewExportController
        └── settingsStore
```

`RootView` reads auth state from `AppCoordinator` and routes to: `AuthView` → `DeviceCodeView` → authenticated shell.

### Shell layers

`AuthenticatedShellView` (in `Shell/`) is the container for the authenticated experience. It wraps `CloudLibraryView` as the primary content. `GamePassShellView`/`MainTabView` provide ambient background and top-chrome overlay.

### CloudLibrary feature (largest feature slice)

```
CloudLibraryView              ← coordinator-connected entry
  └── CloudLibraryShellHost   ← layout + action routing owner
        ├── CloudLibraryShellView       ← side rail + content host
        ├── CloudLibraryContentRouteHost← routes to browse/utility/detail
        ├── CloudLibraryBrowseRouteHost ← home/library/search/consoles
        └── CloudLibraryUtilityRouteHost← profile/settings overlays
```

**State objects (all @MainActor, @Observable):**
- `CloudLibraryViewModel` — source of truth for all library data projections
- `CloudLibrarySceneModel` — scene-level derived state (routes, hero bg, status)
- `CloudLibraryPresentationStore` — presentation projection cache
- `CloudLibraryRouteState` — current browse/utility/detail routes
- `CloudLibraryFocusState` — focus request tokens and settled tile state
- `CloudLibraryLoadState` — loading/error/success envelope

**Data shaping (`Data/CloudLibrary/`):** All transformation from raw library models to view state is side-effect-free and has no async work. These functions are pure and testable without mocks.

### Action routing

`CloudLibraryShellHost` owns the three routed action bags directly through its `browseActions`, `detailActions`, and `utilityActions` computed properties. The former `CloudLibraryActionFactory` passthrough seam is already dissolved.

`CloudLibraryBrowseRouteActions`, `CloudLibraryDetailRouteActions`, and `CloudLibraryUtilityRouteActions` remain the correct boundary types. Keep closures in these routed action structs explicitly `@MainActor` when they are invoked from `@MainActor` UI code.

### Streaming feature

```
StreamView
  └── StreamModalControllerHost
        ├── StreamOverlay (overlay controls + diagnostics)
        └── RenderSurfaceCoordinator
              └── RendererAttachmentCoordinator (@MainActor)
                    ├── MetalVideoRenderer (Integration/WebRTC/)
                    └── SampleBufferDisplayRenderer (series of extensions)
```

`RendererAttachmentCoordinator` is `@MainActor` and manages renderer selection, lifecycle, and fallback. The UIKit/probe support types now live under `Features/Streaming/Rendering/UIKitAdapters/`, leaving the coordinator focused on policy and attachment work.

### Package roles

| Package | Role | Key constraint |
|---------|------|----------------|
| `NorthstarCore` | App lifecycle, auth, controllers, hydration | Owns `AppCoordinator`. No UI. |
| `NorthstarModels` | Shared model types | No dependencies on other packages |
| `XCloudAPI` | Network layer — xCloud API, auth, catalog | No UI |
| `StreamingCore` | WebRTC session, SDP/ICE, channels | No Metal, no UIKit |
| `VideoRenderingKit` | Upscale strategy resolution | No UIKit, no Metal directly |
| `InputBridge` | Gamepad input, input queue | No UI |
| `DiagnosticsKit` | Metrics pipeline, logging, telemetry | No UI |

Packages do not depend on the app target. The app target depends on packages. Packages may depend on each other only along the data-flow direction (NorthstarCore → XCloudAPI, StreamingCore; not the reverse).

### WebRTC integration

`Integration/WebRTC/` is the boundary layer between the WebRTC binary framework and the rest of the app. Everything in this directory is conditionally compiled with `#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE`. Outside this directory, the app uses protocol abstractions from `StreamingCore` and `NorthstarCore`.

---

## Concurrency Model (Layered Actor Strategy)

This project uses a **layered actor strategy**. "Everything is MainActor" is not the model. "Nonisolated by default" is not the model.

**Layer 1 — UI and navigation (@MainActor)**
All SwiftUI views, all view models (`CloudLibraryViewModel`, `CloudLibrarySceneModel`, etc.), all focus/route state. These are `@MainActor` and must remain so. Do not add background threading to UI state without explicit justification.

**Layer 2 — Service and cache (isolated actors)**
`RemoteImagePipeline` in `Shared/Theme/RemoteImagePipeline.swift` is a correct example: an `actor` that owns a mutable cache and an in-flight deduplication dictionary. New shared, mutable, cross-cutting state belongs in a named actor, not in a `nonisolated` class protected by `NSLock` unless benchmark evidence requires it.

**Layer 3 — Rendering and compute (explicit concurrency)**
Metal rendering runs off the main thread via `MTKViewDelegate` callbacks. Heavy async work (image decoding, frame processing) must use `@concurrent` when called from `@MainActor` context. Do not mark rendering code `@MainActor` unless it is purely UI.

**Cross-boundary closures:** All action closures that originate in `@MainActor` view code must be annotated `@MainActor (...) -> Void` to make isolation explicit. Do not use untyped `@escaping` closures at `@MainActor` boundaries.

---

### Test targets

| Target | Framework | Scope |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `NorthstarTests` | XCTest (migrating to Swift Testing) | Unit tests for state, routing, data shaping, focus, streaming |
| `NorthstarUITests` | XCTest (XCUI) | Shell checkpoint captures |
| `NorthstarPerformanceTests` | XCTest | Launch, route switch, post-stream freshness |
| `NorthstarPerformanceUITests` | XCTest | Performance UI scenarios |
| Per-package `Tests/` | Swift Testing (new) / XCTest (existing) | Package-level unit tests |

### Rules

1. **Swift Testing** (`import Testing`) is the target framework for new pure-Swift unit tests. Migrate existing XCTest unit tests incrementally when touching a file.
2. **XCTest + XCUI** must remain for all UI automation. Swift Testing does not replace XCUI.
3. **No mocking the WebRTC layer** in unit tests. Use `#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE` guards and test against the mock/stub path.
4. **Data shaping tests** (`Data/CloudLibrary/`) are pure function tests — no async, no mocks needed.
5. **Performance tests** use the dedicated `Northstar-Perf` scheme.

### CI workflows (`.github/workflows/`)

| Workflow | What it validates |
|----------|------------------|
| `ci-app-build-and-smoke.yml` | Full app build + `AppSmokeTests` |
| `ci-packages.yml` | All SPM package tests |

These are the rules all agents in this repo must follow. They are not optional.

### Structural agreements

1. **Do not create new files without justification.** The project already has a large source surface. New files must represent a genuinely new seam, not a preference for smaller files.
2. **Do not split files unless the split resolves a mixed-responsibility root.** Over-splitting is already an identified problem. Creating additional micro-shards makes it worse.
3. **Do not merge files unless the merge removes an artificial seam.** Merge only what is identified in the Floor/Execution contracts or a newly approved cleanup wave.
4. **Reference images must live in one canonical location.** `Apps/Northstar/Tools/shell-visual-regression/reference/` is the canonical location. Do not create a second reference image directory.
5. **Remove `.DS_Store` files** if encountered. Do not commit them.

### Code agreements

6. **Strict concurrency is always on.** Every new type must declare its isolation. If you add a class, decide: `@MainActor`, actor, or nonisolated with explicit Sendable conformance.
7. **`#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE` guards are mandatory** in `Integration/WebRTC/`. Do not remove them or add WebRTC symbol references outside this directory.
8. **Do not add `@unchecked Sendable`** without a comment explaining why the type cannot conform normally and what invariant makes it safe.
9. **Action closures at UI boundaries** must be annotated `@MainActor` when the closure will be called from `@MainActor` context.
10. **`Task { @MainActor in ... }` is a smell at call sites** in view code. If you are wrapping a UI update in a detached Task inside a view, reconsider whether the caller should be async or whether the state object needs an actor boundary.

### Testing agreements

12. **New unit tests for state machines** go under `NorthstarTests/` with a name matching the type under test (e.g., `CloudLibraryRouteStateTests.swift` for `CloudLibraryRouteState`).
13. **Do not add XCTest unit tests to targets that are migrating to Swift Testing.** Only add Swift Testing tests.
14. **Do not change the CI workflow files** without understanding what guards they enforce. If a workflow must change, document the reason in a comment in the file.

### Package agreements

15. **Packages do not import the app target.** The dependency direction is always app → package, never package → app.
16. **`NorthstarModels` has no package dependencies.** It must remain the leaf-level shared model package.
17. **New model types** that are shared across packages go in `NorthstarModels`, not in the app target.
18. **New network types** go in `XCloudAPI`, not in the app target.
19. **New diagnostic/metrics types** go in `DiagnosticsKit`, not in the app target.

23: /// Resolves the best available upscale strategy for the current device and source dimensions.
24: ///
25: /// The resolver is stateless and cheap to call — run it once whenever source resolution
26: /// changes (i.e. in `configurePresentationResources`, not per frame).
27: ///
28: /// Usage:
29: /// ```swift
30: /// let resolver = UpscaleCapabilityResolver(probe: LiveUpscaleCapabilityProbe())
31: /// let strategy = resolver.resolve(device: device,
32: ///                                 sourceW: 1920, sourceH: 1080,
33: ///                                 targetW: 3840, targetH: 2160)
34: /// ```
35: public struct UpscaleCapabilityResolver: Sendable {
36: 
37:     public let probe: any UpscaleCapabilityProbing
38: 
39:     public init(probe: any UpscaleCapabilityProbing) {
40:         self.probe = probe
41:     }
42:

44:     ///
45:     /// - Returns `.passthrough` when `source >= target` in both dimensions or no upscaler is available.
46:     public func resolve(device: any MTLDevice,
47:                         sourceW: Int, sourceH: Int,
48:                         targetW: Int, targetH: Int) -> UpscaleStrategy {
49:         resolveCandidateResolution(
50:             device: device,
51:             sourceW: sourceW,
52:             sourceH: sourceH,
53:             targetW: targetW,
54:             targetH: targetH
55:         ).candidates.first ?? .passthrough
56:     }
57: 
58:     /// Returns all eligible strategies in descending priority order for the given device and dimensions.
59:     public func resolveCandidates(
60:         device: any MTLDevice,
61:         sourceW: Int,
62:         sourceH: Int,
63:         targetW: Int,
64:         targetH: Int
65:     ) -> [UpscaleStrategy] {

81:     ) -> UpscaleCandidateResolution {

226:         sourceH: Int,

# Skill: ios-autonomous-dev

# ios-autonomous-dev

Field manual for agents doing Apple-platform development without a human at
the IDE. Every rule below was paid for. When a new trap bites in any
project, ADD IT HERE (keep project-specific server/wire details in that
repo's own GOTCHAS.md — this file is only the transferable layer).

## project setup

- **Never edit `.xcodeproj` by hand — generate it.** xcodegen (`project.yml`)
  or tuist; the pbxproj is gitignored output. Hand-edited pbxproj is the #1
  agent failure mode: merge hell, silent setting drift, unreviewable diffs.
- **Non-trivial Info.plist entries need a real plist.** `INFOPLIST_KEY_*`
  build settings cover only a blessed subset. `CFBundleURLTypes` (URL
  schemes), background modes, etc. require xcodegen's target `info:` block —
  which generates an Info.plist and CONFLICTS with
  `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES`. Move launch-screen/orientation keys into
  `info.properties` in the same change.
- **Split protocol/domain logic into an SPM package with zero UI imports.**
  `swift test` on a package is seconds; xcodebuild is tens of seconds to
  minutes. The narrowest verification loop is the one you'll actually run
  after every change. App target = views + glue only.
- **One build driver per session.** `xcodebuild` CLI and Xcode.app destroy
  each other's incremental state in shared DerivedData. Headless work uses
  CLI; if Xcode.app is open and building, drive it instead. Cache-drift
  self-heal: `xcrun simctl shutdown all && rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<App>-*`.
  Concrete failure signature: CLI build dies instantly with `unable to attach
  DB ... build.db: database is locked` — Xcode.app is open (a project regen
  pokes it into re-indexing the same DerivedData). Quit Xcode for headless
  phases; reopen only for mcpbridge-dependent tools (RenderPreview,
  DeviceInteraction*).

## the agent dev loop (2026 ecosystem standard — adopt BEFORE grinding)

The build→install→relaunch loop is the 2024 way and it is why iOS agent work
feels 10x worse than web dev. The current stack (each piece proven on an
Xcode 27 beta seed, 2026-07):

- **LSP first: enable sourcekit-lsp in the agent host.** opencode ships it
  OFF by default — `"lsp": true` in opencode.json. For xcodeproj targets add
  `xcode-build-server` (brew) + `xcode-build-server config -project X.xcodeproj
  -scheme X` at repo root (gitignore `buildServer.json` + `.compile`: absolute
  per-machine paths). Type errors then surface inline on EVERY edit-tool call
  in ~1s — the tsserver loop. Requirements: a recent build in DEFAULT
  DerivedData and `EMIT_FRONTEND_COMMAND_LINES=YES` (Xcode 16.3+ stopped
  logging swiftc invocations without it). Files in brand-new targets report
  "No such module" until the target exists in a built graph — expected, not a
  code error. Diagnostics activate on host restart, not mid-session.
- **Hot reload: InjectionLite + HotSwiftUI (johnno1962), no external app.**
  Recipe: both SPM packages on the app target; Debug-only
  `OTHER_LDFLAGS: $(inherited) -Xlinker -interposable`;
  EMIT_FRONTEND_COMMAND_LINES=YES; per-view `@ObserveInjection private var
  inject` + `.enableInjection()` LAST in the body chain (release = no-op);
  launch with `SIMCTL_CHILD_INJECTION_DIRECTORIES=<repo>` via
  `simctl launch --console-pty` in a persistent session so the 💉 lines are
  visible. Watcher parses the newest xcactivitylog in DEFAULT DerivedData —
  never `-derivedDataPath` the dev-loop build, and
  `COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING` breaks it. Measured on a 27-beta sim:
  save → recompile 742ms → interpose → SwiftUI redraw, state + presented
  alerts intact. Root-level observers only redraw the root's own body — every
  view gets its own observer or its edits won't repaint.
- **Token-cheap builds: pipe xcodebuild through `xcsift`** (brew). Whole
  build report as ~50-token JSON (status/errors/warnings) vs pages of
  xcbeautify. Keep xcbeautify for humans, xcsift for agent loops.
- **Snapshot tests (pointfree swift-snapshot-testing) as the fast pixel
  tier**: hosting-controller renders at unit-test speed, PNG artifacts an
  agent can Read. LIMIT: Liquid Glass materials do not render on this path —
  pin layout/content/state with snapshots; material/feel truth stays with
  RenderPreview and on-sim screenshots. A scratch "verification" test the
  agent retargets at any view beats booting the app for single-view looks.
- **Guardrails in config, not prose**: deny agent edits to `*.pbxproj` /
  `*.xcodeproj/*` at the permission layer. The #1 ecosystem failure mode.
- **Beta toolchains outrun released automation tools.** Xcode 27 beta moved
  SimulatorKit.framework (Developer/Library/PrivateFrameworks →
  Contents/SharedFrameworks); every released binary that dlopen'd the old
  path broke (AXe ≤1.7.1 etc). Before adopting any sim-automation tool on a
  beta: check the repo's main-branch compatibility statement against your
  exact seed, expect to build from source when the release predates the
  seed (the project's own Makefile, not CI-artifact spelunking). brew "CLT
  too outdated" on tap formulae is a preflight gate — prebuilt release
  tarballs sidestep it.

## simulator automation

- **ATS's localhost exemption hides plain-HTTP breakage until the first
  real device.** Simulators talk to 127.0.0.1, which App Transport
  Security exempts — every sim test passes, then the device's first
  non-localhost `http://` call dies with "requires the use of a secure
  connection". If the backend is deliberately plain HTTP (private
  tailnet/VPN mesh), declare `NSAppTransportSecurity` →
  `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` (or scoped exceptions) BEFORE the first device
  install, and test-drive against a NON-localhost host on the sim at least
  once.

- **`simctl openurl` with a custom URL scheme triggers a SpringBoard
  "Open in <app>?" dialog** that persists across app relaunches and cannot
  be dismissed headlessly. Custom schemes are NOT a scripting hook from
  outside the app. A stuck SpringBoard alert clears with a sim reboot
  (`simctl shutdown <udid> && simctl boot <udid>`).
- **Deterministic navigation hook: launch arguments.** `-key value` launch
  args auto-populate `UserDefaults` — `simctl launch booted <bundle>
  -myapp.tab fleet` + a 3-line read in the root view gives scripted
  screenshot runs and XCUITest a stable entry point. Build this into every
  app on day one.
- **Never mix build-and-run helpers with argumented launches.** Tools that
  build+install+launch in one shot (xcodebuildmcp build-and-run) fire their
  own arg-less launch which can race or replace your later
  `simctl launch <bundle> -args…`, leaving an instance WITHOUT your launch
  args on screen while logs gaslight you. When args matter: build with
  `-derivedDataPath`, `simctl install` the .app, then launch exactly once
  yourself. Diagnose with `simctl spawn <udid> launchctl list | grep
  <bundle>` + an os_log line at arg-parse time.
- **Headless sims have no window to click.** Tooling like xcodebuildmcp
  boots sims without Simulator.app, so window-automation tools (cua-driver
  etc.) have nothing to target, and opening Simulator.app steals user
  focus. Interaction ladder: launch args → accessibility-id-driven XCUITest
  → only then window automation.
- **Seed app state through the app's own persistence files.**
  `xcrun simctl get_app_container booted <bundle> data` → write into
  `Library/Application Support/...` before launch. Faster and more honest
  than UI-driving through setup flows for every scripted run.
- **`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` builds are compile-checks, NEVER installables.**
  `simctl install` of an unsigned .app half-registers: placeholder grid
  icon with an installing dot, process spawns on launch but SpringBoard
  never foregrounds it — and the wedged registration SURVIVES uninstall +
  signed reinstall. Recovery: `simctl uninstall` → `simctl shutdown` +
  `boot` (SpringBoard state reset) → install the SIGNED build (sim default
  ad-hoc signing; just drop the flag). Keep two build invocations: flagged
  for CI checks, unflagged with `-derivedDataPath` for installs.
- **Always `simctl terminate` BEFORE `simctl install` on iOS 27 sims.**
  Installing over a running instance intermittently wedges SpringBoard the
  same way (placeholder icon, FBSOpenApplicationServiceErrorDomain code 4
  on launch). The reliable install loop is: terminate → install → seed →
  launch. If wedged anyway: uninstall → shutdown → boot → install.
- **Screenshot verification is mandatory and adversarial.** Build → run →
  screenshot → actually LOOK. Screenshots of plausible-but-wrong data read
  as success (a fallback field can mask a wrong key and the pixels still
  look right). Verify the DATA in the pixels against the source of truth,
  not just "screen looks reasonable".
- **Beta-era tool drift is constant.** Subcommands drift (`build-and-run`
  takes `--simulator-name`, `screenshot` only `--simulator-id`); frameworks
  vanish (SimulatorKit → UI-snapshot tools break). Check `<tool>
  <subcommand> --help` on first use each session; after an Xcode update,
  suspect the seed before the code.
- **Beta Xcodes ship without the Metal Toolchain.** Any dependency that
  compiles .metal shaders (SwiftTerm's renderer, most graphics packages)
  fails with `cannot execute tool 'metal'`. Fix is a one-time
  `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain` (multi-GB — run it
  detached and keep working on non-Xcode surfaces while it pulls).

## verification loops

- **Formatters invalidate your memory of the file.** If swiftformat (or any
  formatter) ran since you last read a region, your remembered text is
  stale — exact-match edits will half-match reformatted code and leave
  orphaned fragments (duplicate struct tails, stray braces). Re-read the
  exact region immediately before structural edits, prefer replacing whole
  top-level declarations over mid-body slices, and rebuild right after any
  large replacement to catch brace damage while the diff is fresh.
- **Xcode 27 ships official agent skills — export them before heavy SwiftUI
  work**: `xcrun mcpbridge run-agent skills export --output-dir <path>`
  (requires Xcode.app running). `swiftui-whats-new-27` is authoritative on
  2027 API changes (notably: `@State` became a MACRO in SDK 27 — its compile
  errors have a documented correct fix and an "obvious" WRONG one; consult
  the skill's references, never fix from training memory).
  `device-interaction` documents Apple's sanctioned sim/device driving:
  `DeviceInteractionStartSession → DeviceInteractionInstallAndRun →
  DeviceEventSynthesize` (touch synthesis + UI hierarchy + screenshots via
  the Xcode MCP / mcpbridge) — prefer it over ad-hoc window automation when
  the Xcode MCP is connected.
- **Order of verification: package tests → app build (one platform) → both
  platforms → sim run + screenshots.** Never run the expensive loop when
  the cheap one hasn't passed.
- **Every reusable view gets `#Preview` with representative states**
  (loading/empty/populated/error) backed by a fixtures file. Previews are
  the visual feedback loop; no preview = flying blind on that view.
- **Accessibility identifiers on every interactive element from day one**
  (`{surface}_{context}_{element}`). They're the UI-automation contract AND
  real accessibility; retrofitting them later is misery.
- **Gate live-server integration suites behind an env var** with Swift
  Testing traits: `.enabled(if: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["X"] ==
  "1")` plus `.timeLimit(...)` so a wedged server can't hang CI. Default
  `swift test` stays hermetic and fast.
- **`swift test --filter` matches TYPE names, not display names.**
  `--filter "My Suite Name"` silently matches nothing (easy-to-miss "No
  matching test cases were run" warning); filter on the struct/class name.
- **zsh pipe status is `$pipestatus` (lowercase array)**, not bash's
  `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` — exit-code checks on `xcodebuild | xcbeautify`
  silently evaluate empty otherwise.
- **Journal every detached daemon you spawn** (dev servers, automation
  daemons) and reap them at checkpoint time. Orphans hold ports and poison
  later runs with stale state.
- **Booted simulators are silent CPU hogs** — especially with an installed
  app reconnect-looping against a dead backend (SSE backoff churn burns a
  core indefinitely). `xcrun simctl shutdown all` belongs in every
  session-end/checkpoint sweep alongside daemon reaping. Two idle-looking
  sims + one dead server pegged a Mac at 100%.

## API clients / streaming (the transferable patterns)

- **The spec is the map; the wire is the territory.** Draft models from the
  vendored OpenAPI doc, then capture REAL responses/frames from a live
  server and pin verbatim captures as decode tests before trusting
  `required`/optionality. Generated specs drift from wire behavior,
  especially on envelope fields and free-form `object` blobs.
- **Synthetic fixtures inherit your assumptions; captures don't.** A
  hand-written fixture happily encodes the same wrong guess as the model
  it tests (string where the wire has an object) and passes forever. Every
  decodable aggregate gets at least one verbatim live-capture test, with an
  assertion that no element fell through to the unknown/passthrough case —
  that's the drift alarm.
- **Audit captures for personal data before committing them as fixtures.**
  Live servers return real user state (session titles, paths, transcripts).
  Filter to harness-generated records and grep for the user's name/home
  paths before a capture lands in git.
- **Evaluate codegen on union shape before adopting it.** `jq` the schema:
  a large `anyOf`/`oneOf` WITHOUT `discriminator` means generators emit
  trial-decode-every-variant types — poison on streaming hot paths and
  unusable ergonomics. Uniform tagged envelopes (`{type, payload}`) want a
  hand-written O(1) switch with an `.unknown` passthrough case for forward
  compatibility.
- **Audit "read" endpoints for side effects before polling them.** Routing
  headers/params that scope requests to a workspace/instance can CREATE
  that instance server-side. Only query scopes proven to exist; a
  reconciliation loop must never be able to spawn resources.
- **Decode failures must not kill a stream.** Log + skip undecodable
  frames; cover gaps with periodic/RE-connect REST reconciliation. A poison
  frame that errors the stream = reconnect storm against the same frame.
- **`URLSession.timeoutIntervalForRequest` is an idle-byte timer on
  `bytes(for:)` streams** — it resets on every byte. Set it to ~2.5× the
  server's heartbeat interval and silent link death surfaces as a timeout
  error in bounded time. Without it, dead SSE links linger for 60s+.
- **Live events + REST reconciliation on every (re)connect** is the resync
  contract for any push client: never assume a frame was seen; on connect,
  re-read server truth and merge (items that arrived after the fetch began
  survive absence from the fetched list).
- **Optimistic mutations restore on failure.** Remove locally → POST → on
  error re-insert + surface. The server's confirming event is the
  authoritative clear — and it must also clear state when OTHER clients
  perform the action.
- **`AsyncStream` is single-consumer.** Fan-out needs a continuation
  registry (dict keyed by UUID, cleaned in `onTermination`). Yield current
  state immediately on subscribe so late subscribers aren't blank.
- **Inject a clock** (`now: () -> Date`) into anything that orders by
  arrival time; wall-clock ordering assertions are flaky under test.
- **Server processes cache config at startup.** Test harnesses that write
  config files must (re)start the server AFTER writing, then poll for the
  expected behavior instead of assuming it.

## provisioning realities (free developer account)

- Free accounts: 7-day signing expiry, no push entitlements
  (`aps-environment` forbidden), no APNs. Design the awareness stack on
  local notifications + background refresh + (on macOS) unrestricted
  always-on processes. Auto-redeploy tooling (`devicectl` install over
  wi-fi on a cron) is core infrastructure, not a hack — build the expiry
  countdown into the app itself.
- CLI builds for CI/verification: `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` builds succeed
  without a team; anything that must RUN on device/sim gets signed
  ad-hoc/personal-team at install time. Keychain APIs
  (`kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain`) need a signed binary at runtime — CLI
  unsigned builds compile fine but can't exercise them.

## design-direction work with previews (added 2026-07-19, boxbox redesign)

- **RenderPreview (mcpbridge) is the ONLY autonomous path that renders
  real Liquid Glass.** Snapshot tests through UIHostingController silently
  draw glass as flat fills — fine for layout pins, a LIE for material/
  design judgment. Pitch visuals via `#Preview` + RenderPreview; keep a
  scratch previews file in the app target for concept work.
- **Multi-frame flow strips beat single screens for UX sign-off.** A
  `#Preview(traits: .fixedLayout(width:~1200, height:~700))` canvas with
  3-4 scaled phone frames (`.scaleEffect` + fixed frame), numbered
  captions ("you tap X → Y happens"), and arrows reads as a usable
  journey. Users reject isolated screens they can't navigate mentally.
- **Test runs via Xcode/mcpbridge inherit the ACTIVE run destination** —
  a physical-device destination breaks test-bundle signing on free teams.
  Switch to a simulator destination first, restore the user's destination
  after. Unit-test bundles also need `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES`
  (xcodegen won't add it for you).
- **Blurred-shape backdrops must be `.overlay` on a sized base, never
  ZStack siblings** — an oversized blurred Circle/Ellipse inflates the
  ZStack's layout size and the whole canvas renders shifted/cropped.
  Gradient base → `.overlay { blobs }` → `.clipped()`.
- **fontWidth(.compressed/.expanded) works on system fonts** — the fast
  path to broadcast/instrument display type without bundling fonts.

## agent-shell process discipline (added 2026-07-19, wave harness)

- **Backgrounded children die with the one-shot shell (SIGHUP).** `serve &`
  or `(curl ... &)` inside a single agent exec call gets killed the moment
  the shell exits — "started fine, dead one command later". Bit twice in
  one session (a cmx serve, then a long-poll curl that silently never sent
  its request). Anything that must outlive the call gets a REAL daemon
  spawn (agent runtime detach mode / setsid) — and journal the pid so you
  reap it before the session ends.
- **agent-device refs are per-snapshot; any mutation rebinds them.** A ref
  from snapshot N pressed after the tree changed resolves to the WRONG
  element (observed: "chip" ref landing on a masthead icon, misread as an
  app filter bug). Rule: snapshot -i, act on ITS refs immediately, then
  diff snapshot to verify; after any state change, re-snapshot before the
  next press. Never chain a press behind another mutating command in one
  shell line.
- **Don't screencapture/AppleScript-probe the host Mac from inside the
  agent terminal without need** — each new probe path (osascript → System
  Events, direct screencapture) can throw a SYSTEM consent dialog onto the
  user's screen that you cannot dismiss without the very permission it
  asks for. Prefer the platform automation stack (agent-device) and fall
  back to window-region capture only with coordinates you already hold.

1: //
2: //  CASShader.metal
3: //  Northstar
4: //
5: //  NV12 → BGRA compute kernel for the Metal video pipeline.
6: //  Handles both full-range (420f) and limited-range (420v) input detected per-frame.
7: //
8: //  Input:
9: //    texture(0)  yPlane    — R8Unorm,  full-resolution luma (Y plane of NV12)
10: //    texture(1)  cbcrPlane — RG8Unorm, half-resolution chroma (CbCr plane of NV12)
11: //    buffer(2)   isFullRange — uint32, 1 = 420f (full range), 0 = 420v (limited range)
12: //
13: //  Output:
14: //    texture(2)  output    — BGRA8Unorm, full-resolution linear RGB frame
15: //
16: //  Pipeline:
17: //    WebRTC frame (RTCCVPixelBuffer NV12)
18: //      ↓ CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage (zero-copy)
19: //      ↓ nv12ToBGRA compute shader (NV12 → BGRA, BT.709, auto range)
20: //      ↓ optional MTLFXSpatialScaler (frame → display-sized texture)
21: //      ↓ blit to MTKView drawable
22: //
23: 
24: #include <metal_stdlib>
25: using namespace metal;
26: 
27: // MARK: - NV12 → RGB (BT.709, range-aware)
28: //
29: // fullRange = true  → 420f: Y in [0,1] maps to [0,255], UV centre-only offset.
30: // fullRange = false → 420v: Y in [0,1] maps to [16,235] (studio swing).
31: //
32: // xCloud H.264 streams: RTCVideoDecoderH264 currently hardcodes 420f output.
33: // Once patch 0003 lands (decoder → 420v), fullRange will be false in production.
34: static float3 nv12ToRGB(float y, float2 cbcr, bool fullRange) {
35:     float yS, cb, cr;
36:     if (fullRange) {
37:         // Full range: Y directly usable, UV only needs centre offset.
38:         yS = y;
39:         cb = cbcr.x - 128.0 / 255.0;
40:         cr = cbcr.y - 128.0 / 255.0;
41:     } else {
42:         // Limited range (studio swing): rescale Y [16-235] and UV [16-240].
43:         yS = (y     - 16.0  / 255.0) * (255.0 / 219.0);
44:         cb = (cbcr.x - 128.0 / 255.0) * (255.0 / 224.0);
45:         cr = (cbcr.y - 128.0 / 255.0) * (255.0 / 224.0);
46:     }
47: 
48:     // BT.709 matrix (identical for both ranges — only the Y/UV scaling differs above).
49:     float r = yS                + 1.5748 * cr;
50:     float g = yS - 0.1873 * cb - 0.4681 * cr;
51:     float b = yS + 1.8556 * cb;
52: 
53:     return clamp(float3(r, g, b), 0.0, 1.0);
54: }
55: 
56: // MARK: - Passthrough kernel
57: 
58: kernel void nv12ToBGRA(
59:     texture2d<float, access::read>  yPlane      [[texture(0)]],
60:     texture2d<float, access::read>  cbcrPlane   [[texture(1)]],
61:     texture2d<float, access::write> output      [[texture(2)]],
62:     constant uint32_t              &isFullRange  [[buffer(2)]],
63:     uint2 gid [[thread_position_in_grid]]
64: ) {
65:     if (gid.x >= output.get_width() || gid.y >= output.get_height()) { return; }
66: 
67:     float  y    = yPlane.read(gid).r;
68:     float2 cbcr = cbcrPlane.read(uint2(gid.x / 2, gid.y / 2)).rg;
69: 
70:     float3 rgb = nv12ToRGB(y, cbcr, isFullRange != 0);
71:     output.write(float4(rgb, 1.0), gid);
72: }

parts.text:
Now I'm moving to VideoRenderingKit, rewriting the upscale strategy, capability resolver, live probe, and render ladder planner along with their tests. I'm defining an enum for upscale strategies covering MetalFX spatial upscaling and VideoToolbox super resolution options.

I'm sketching a protocol for probing upscaler capabilities and a preference enum for choosing between automatic, MetalFX, or VideoToolbox super resolution. I decide to drop a "none" case since the existing upscaling toggle already handles that, so a passthrough Metal draw is visually equivalent to letting the compositor scale via the sample buffer path.

Now I'm designing a resolver that orders candidate upscaling paths based on the chosen preference, always falling back to passthrough last, and a planner that decides between a sample-buffer floor and a Metal-renderer floor when the primary upscaler isn't available — for instance if MetalFX gets thermally demoted.

The Metal floor avoids a view switch, giving a smoother transition versus the sample floor's flash, so I'm leaning toward making metalFloor the default even though that changes a user-visible diagnostics setting — but I want to double check there isn't a thermal cost tradeoff, since a Metal passthrough still means a full 4K drawable write each frame.

Actually, the sample layer runs at source resolution so it's cheaper for the compositor, which makes it the better choice during thermal demotion. So the policy becomes: thermal demotion falls back to sample floor since it's cheapest, while a MetalFX failure falls back to whatever floor the setting specifies — keeping sampleFloor as the default is the minimal change. I'll keep the nextCandidate and deadRungs helpers as they are, and now I need to look at the UpscaleCapabilityResolverTests file to see what it currently covers before rewriting it to drop the metal4fx/llfi cases and align with Swift Testing.

+    /// Re-baselines two stream defaults whose meaning changed with the paced render pipeline:
+    /// "Low Latency Mode" now trades frame pacing for input latency (previously it only doubled
+    /// keyframe requests), and audio boost no longer defaults to +3 dB of saturating gain.
+    /// Runs once; users who explicitly change either setting afterwards keep their choice.
+    @discardableResult
+    private nonisolated static func migratePacingDefaults(
+        defaults: UserDefaults,
+        appDomainName: String
+    ) -> Bool {
+        guard !defaults.bool(forKey: Key.pacingDefaultsMigrationKey) else { return false }
+        defer { defaults.set(true, forKey: Key.pacingDefaultsMigrationKey) }
+
+        let domain = defaults.persistentDomain(forName: appDomainName) ?? [:]
+        var migrated = false
+        if domain[Key.lowLatencyMode] != nil {
+            defaults.set(false, forKey: Key.lowLatencyMode)
+            migrated = true
+        }
+        if domain[Key.audioBoost] != nil {
+            defaults.set(0.0, forKey: Key.audioBoost)
+            migrated = true
+        }
+        return migrated
+    }

Now I'm tackling the big rewrite of MetalVideoRenderer, starting to lay out the Swift file with the necessary imports for Metal, MetalFX, CoreVideo, and AVFoundation under the appropriate platform conditions.

I'm designing the renderer class conforming to RTCVideoRenderer, which converts NV12 frames to BGRA and optionally upscales via MetalFX, presenting on a dedicated thread paced by CAMetalDisplayLink. I'm working through how to safely handle the telemetry and candidate callbacks—weighing whether to pass them in as closures at init versus mutable properties set after, since the coordinator currently assigns them post-init before frames arrive but also reassigns on updates, so I need a thread-safe way to store them.

Since the coordinator's rendererCallbacks struct gets recreated each SwiftUI pass, I'm deciding to assign the renderer's own closures only once during install(), having them capture a stable pump continuation, while the actual callback object gets swapped separately via a main-actor `callbacks` var that the pump handler reads from. I'm also sketching out the lock-protected shared state—latest frame with arrival time and sequence number, pending render request, and various frame counters—alongside render-thread-only state that never crosses the lock boundary.

Now I'm thinking about the render thread setup itself: a Thread subclass running its own loop, with a CAMetalDisplayLink created there. But CAMetalDisplayLink requires the metal layer, which belongs to the view on the main thread, and I'm trying to recall whether Apple's WWDC23 guidance creates the display link on main and then attaches it to the render thread's run loop, or does it differently.

Apple's sample actually creates the display link on main using the layer, then calls add(to:forMode:) from within the render thread itself to attach it to that thread's run loop -- I'll follow that pattern. The delegate callback then fires on whichever thread owns that run loop, giving me access to the drawable and timing info I need for scheduling frames.

In the callback, I lock to grab the latest frame and pending request, then check if the frame's sequence differs from the last presented one -- if there's nothing new, I just return without presenting, since skipping a present simply leaves the previous content on screen. For pacing, I'm distinguishing between a smooth "paced" mode that only presents at display-link callbacks versus an "immediate" low-latency mode that renders and presents as soon as a frame arrives.

For immediate mode, I'll dispatch work to the render thread's run loop and use nextDrawable, accepting that it may briefly block since it's on a dedicated thread. Rather than trying to coordinate the display link with immediate mode, I'll simply make the callback a no-op and pause the display link when in immediate mode, since frames are presented as they arrive anyway -- so I'll expose this as a presentationMode option with paced and immediate cases. In paced mode, the present call relies on the display link having already timed the callback so the frame lands on the target vsync, as long as the GPU work finishes in time.

For latency, presenting ASAP right after GPU completion works fine since the display link just paces when decisions happen, not when frames are shown — the frame lands at the next vsync after it's ready. I'll go with plain present(drawable) rather than a scheduled time, since pacing at decision-time already keeps us in sync while minimizing added delay.

With preferredFrameLatency=1, the callback fires roughly one frame ahead of the target vsync, so frames arriving after that pickup point get pushed to the following vsync, averaging about +8.3ms latency versus immediate mode. The tradeoff is that paced mode avoids double-rendering per vsync and smooths out jitter — if frames arrive irregularly, immediate mode can show inconsistent timing while paced absorbs that variance.

Since network jitter is already smoothed by the WebRTC jitter buffer, immediate mode's real advantage is its lower average latency, around 8ms. The bigger question is whether Moonlight's default immediate submission still causes judder from decode/render timing variability interacting with vsync pickup, since the smoothness issue traced back mainly to main-thread scheduling rather than presentation mode itself.

This is basically what AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer's control timebase or Moonlight's frame pacing does — holding a small queue and releasing one frame per vsync so bursts get delayed rather than dropped, trading latency for smoothness. For Metal, I'd implement this as a bounded queue of 2-3 decoded frames, presenting the oldest at each display tick and dropping the oldest if the queue overflows to keep latency in check.

So: `.smooth` mode uses that display-link-driven pacing queue, while `.lowLatency` mode presents immediately with latest-wins semantics and no queuing. I should also confirm this handles lower frame rates like 30fps gracefully, since the queue would just get filled every other tick without issue.

For the actual queue structure, I'm keeping a locked array of pending frames capped at depth 2 — appending on render and dropping the oldest if it overflows, with the display link callback popping the front. I also want to pause the display link entirely when there's no active track or the view is hidden, to save power, and make sure switching between sample layer and Metal output pauses it appropriately too.

For scaler creation, I'm handling MetalFX rebuilds off the main render thread — dispatching to a background queue when resolution or target changes, then delivering the built scaler back via the render thread, with passthrough rendering while the build is in progress since it can take some time for larger upscales.

During that passthrough window, I want to render a simple bilinear-filtered fullscreen quad sampling the output texture directly into the drawable, avoiding any visible layer switch. I'm thinking through whether to add this as a render pipeline or compute kernel in the shader file, and realizing it might be more efficient to skip the BGRA intermediate step and sample the Y and CbCr planes directly into RGB for the drawable in one pass.

For the MetalFX path, I still need the intermediate BGRA texture at source resolution before scaling. I'm working out how to configure the spatial scaler's output texture to point directly at the drawable, checking texture usage compatibility and falling back to an intermediate blit if the drawable's texture doesn't support the required usage flags, and confirming the pixel format matches what the scaler descriptor expects.

Now I'm reasoning through the color processing mode—since MetalFX's perceptual mode expects gamma-encoded input, and our BGRA video is already close to sRGB, that should work fine. I'm also thinking about drawable sizing: whether to set it to the target 4K resolution when upscaling, or keep it at source resolution for the passthrough rung and let the compositor handle scaling.

Weighing the tradeoffs, letting the compositor scale during passthrough is essentially free and comparable quality, while the 4K MetalFX drawable costs about 1-1.5ms GPU for the bilinear pass. I'll keep drawableSize at source resolution during passthrough and switch to 4K only when MetalFX is active, accepting the occasional reallocation hitch when rungs change since that's rare.

For thread safety, I'm setting drawableSize on the render thread wrapped in a CATransaction with actions disabled, since this is common practice for CAMetalLayer even outside the main thread.

Now I'm designing the telemetry system: snapshotting frame stats every second from the render thread (frames received/presented/dropped, queue depth, GPU time, present latency measured via the drawable's presented handler comparing arrival time to presented time), plus processing status and dimensions.

I'm also mapping out thread-safety boundaries for the @unchecked Sendable class -- what's lock-protected (queue, request state, counters), what's render-thread-only (Metal resources, scaler), and what's main-only (the UIKit view) -- documenting this in the class comment. Then I'm planning the RendererAttachmentCoordinator changes: swapping mtkView for layerView, assigning closures once at install, and having update() just refresh callbacks/config and set the display target.

Since UIScreen access needs the main thread, I decide the coordinator itself should compute display target dimensions there and pass them through setRequest, keeping UIKit off the render thread. I'm also working through how resolution changes should behave without resetting the whole ladder -- recomputing the plan and keeping the active rung if it's still eligible, otherwise falling back -- and starting to think through thermal state observation via ProcessInfo.

thermalStateDidChangeNotification to suspend upscaling under load and re-enable it once conditions improve.

Given the low event rates for telemetry and candidate updates, I decide unbounded buffering is safe enough to avoid stalling the ladder, so I'll keep that as-is and move on to thinking through the sample buffer display renderer.

For the renderer, I'm working out how to enqueue frames from the WebRTC thread directly using the new receiver-based API, and pacing PTS through the synchronizer: smooth mode uses a controlled timebase with a small presentation delay, while low-latency mode needs the PTS set essentially to the current host time so frames display at the very next vsync despite the synchronizer being technically "not recommended" for that use case in the docs.

I'm also cleaning up related pieces: only firing dimension-change callbacks when they actually change, allowing two frames in flight for LLSR with session start moved off the decode thread and pre-warmed on a utility queue, dropping the forced telemetry, respecting the fallback flag, and removing the old LLFI code entirely. parts.text:
I'm planning the SampleBufferDisplayRenderer rewrite across multiple files: one handling core state and frame rendering, another managing buffer enqueueing with pacing timestamps and telemetry, and a third handling lifecycle concerns like setting the requested rung and binding.

For low-latency super resolution, I'm designing it to keep two frames in flight with session creation happening off the decode thread, while removing forced per-frame telemetry and dropping frame interpolation entirely along with its file.

For timing, I'm figuring out how the render synchronizer should be created on the main thread during binding, with its rate set against host time so I can compute presentation timestamps as host time plus a delay -- roughly 25ms for smooth playback, or near-zero for low-latency mode.

Since anchoring the synchronizer's rate to host time keeps its timebase tracking the host clock closely, presentation timestamps set to "now" should display at the next vsync as intended. I'm also confirming that display layer access needs to stay on the main actor while the receiver, marked sendable, can be safely stored and used from the WebRTC thread.

Enqueuing frames and flushing the receiver work from any thread since it's sendable. I'm building the ready sample buffer by wrapping the pixel buffer and constructing its dynamic content type...

I'm mapping out the remaining enqueue failure cases—flush-required and generic error cancellations both need to increment a failure counter for later reporting. I'm deciding to skip exposing video performance metrics for now since the renderer is main-actor bound, keeping the scope tighter. For the alternate pixel-buffer processing path, I'm sketching the flow of converting to a destination buffer, wrapping it as a sample buffer, and enqueuing it similarly, while allowing two frames in flight.

Session pre-warming should kick off asynchronously using known source dimensions when the requested rendering rung changes, falling back to lazy creation on first frame if dimensions aren't yet known—frames keep displaying through the plain path meanwhile. I'm designing a method to submit low-latency super-resolution frames from the decode thread, non-blocking, using a state lock to check for a fallback condition before proceeding with the pixel buffer and scale factor.

Then in the processing function, I prepare source and destination buffers and invoke the processor, with success handling that copies attachments, activates display, enqueues the output frame, decrements the in-flight count, and drains any pending frame, while init errors get retried with a bounded backoff window.

Since the completion closure is likely `@Sendable` and captures non-Sendable `CVPixelBuffer` values, I need an `@unchecked Sendable` wrapper struct to bundle the source buffer, destination buffer, arrival time, and resources safely across the boundary.

parts.text:
I'm looking at a data race warning around sending `sampleBuffer` into `CMReadySampleBuffer` at PlainPipeline:133, since the buffer is captured alongside the non-Sendable pixel buffer.  I'm considering whether wrapping the pixel buffer differently, changing `var` to `let`, or other workarounds would satisfy the region-based Sendable checker, since the underlying CMSampleBuffer object itself really isn't reused elsewhere.  The actual conflict traces back to how `pixelBuffer` is used earlier in `renderFrame`, particularly around the low-latency super-resolution submission before `enqueue` is called, so I need to trace whether the pixel buffer is truly free to send by that point.

Since the actual usage is safe, I'm thinking about wrapping the pixel buffer in an `@unchecked Sendable` box class to sidestep the region isolation warning without changing runtime behavior, since boxing a non-Sendable value inside a Sendable wrapper shouldn't itself trigger diagnostics.

Actually, leaving a warning in fresh code isn't ideal, so I'll wrap the pixel buffer handoff in an `@unchecked Sendable` helper class, mirroring the existing `InFlightFrame` pattern, and route buffer creation through it. Then I move on to the main-actor warnings around `metalLayer` access in DrawPipeline and PresentationResources.

Since `MetalVideoLayerView` is a UIView tied to the main actor, its `metalLayer` property is isolated too, so touching it from the render thread triggers warnings. My fix is to grab the `CAMetalLayer` reference during main-actor init and store it directly on the renderer as a plain `let` inside an `@unchecked Sendable` wrapper, since `CAMetalLayer` itself isn't main-actor annotated. That way the render thread can call `nextDrawable()` and read `drawableSize` without ever touching the view again.

Now I'm scanning for the "will never be executed" warning inside the MetalFX-gated spatial scaling code, checking the fallback texture size comparison logic and surrounding lines to figure out which branch is actually dead.

### 4. Rendering Frame Rate

Two renderer paths are available:

| Path | Setting | When used |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `MetalVideoRenderer` (CAS) | `guide.renderer_mode = "metalCAS"` or `"auto"` with sharpness/saturation active | Custom Metal CAS path with image processing |
| `SampleBufferDisplayLayer` | `guide.renderer_mode = "sampleBuffer"` or `"auto"` at neutral settings | Default `AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer` |

**Performance comparison:**
- `SampleBufferDisplayLayer` has lower CPU/GPU overhead — best for battery life
- `MetalVideoRenderer` adds CAS (Contrast Adaptive Sharpening) and saturation processing — small GPU cost but higher perceived quality

**If frames are dropping:**
1. Switch renderer to `sampleBuffer` via guide → Diagnostics to isolate whether it's a Metal rendering issue
2. Check Instruments → Metal GPU Debugger for GPU utilization
3. Lower resolution: 1080p → 720p reduces decoder load
4. Check device temperature — Apple TV throttles CPU/GPU when hot

- `RenderSurfaceCoordinator` records the first-frame milestone separately from connection state
- `RendererAttachmentCoordinator` reports renderer mode changes, candidate failures, and decode failures
- the merged `StreamingStatsSnapshot` includes negotiated dimensions, input flush cadence, and renderer telemetry in addition to raw WebRTC stats

### 5. First-Frame Regressions

The current repo treats "connected" and "first frame" as distinct milestones for a reason. Several failure classes can happen after the peer connection is technically up:

- the video track arrives late
- the renderer attaches to the wrong or stale session identity
- the renderer candidate is chosen but cannot draw
- the overlay/HUD path changes UI state before the first drawable frame arrives

# AGENTS.override.md — Packages/VideoRenderingKit/

VideoRenderingKit owns upscale strategy resolution and render ladder planning. It is queried by `RendererAttachmentCoordinator` in the app target to determine which upscale path to use for a given device.

**Modernization contract reference:** If rendering-strategy work is part of the modernization program, read `Docs/Northstar_Modernization_Contracts.md` together with the modernization plan, monolith breakdown, and file matrix before changing structure or ownership.

---

## Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `UpscaleStrategy.swift` | Enum defining available upscale strategies: Metal4FX, LLSR, LLFI, MetalFX, passthrough. |
| `UpscaleCapabilityResolver.swift` | Detects device capability and resolves the best available strategy. |
| `RenderLadderPlanner.swift` | Plans the render ladder (resolution steps) for a given strategy. |
| `LiveUpscaleCapabilityProbe.swift` | Runtime probe that detects actual GPU/VT capability. |

---

## Upscale priority (documented in MetalVideoRenderer)

```
Metal4FX → LLSR → LLFI → MetalFX → passthrough
```

Capability is detected at runtime via `LiveUpscaleCapabilityProbe`. The resolved strategy is passed to `RendererAttachmentCoordinator.Configuration`.

---

## Rules

1. No UIKit, no SwiftUI, no Metal imports. This package determines strategy; it does not execute rendering.
2. `UpscaleCapabilityResolver` must be callable from `@MainActor` context without blocking. If the probe requires I/O, make it async.
3. `RenderLadderFloorBehavior` is referenced in `RendererAttachmentCoordinator.Configuration`. Keep this type in VideoRenderingKit.
4. Tests live in `Tests/VideoRenderingKitTests/UpscaleCapabilityResolverTests.swift`.

Now I'm putting together the summary: what builds and tests passed, what still needs on-device verification (MetalFX, LLSR, the beta AVSampleBufferVideoRenderer.Receiver API, CAMetalDisplayLink behavior), the behavioral defaults that changed, deferred items, how to A/B test the upscaler on device, and the next steps including the commit offer.

All of it is implemented, building, and unit-tested. Nothing is committed yet (you didn't ask me to) — the work is staged on a new branch `perf/render-pipeline-tvos27`, 60 files, sitting on top of your `154d0b0` local-co-op commit.

## What changed

**Render path (the jank fix)**
- `MetalVideoRenderer` is rewritten: it owns a `CAMetalLayer` (no more `MTKView`) and renders on a **dedicated render thread** driven by `CAMetalDisplayLink`. Nothing on the per-frame path touches the main actor anymore.
- MetalFX spatial now writes **directly into the drawable** (with an automatic intermediate+blit fallback if the drawable's usage bits ever don't allow it) — the 33 MB/frame copy is gone.
- Scaler builds happen on a background queue; frames keep flowing through a bilinear NV12 passthrough pass until the new scaler lands. No more synchronous pipeline compiles on main, and **no more ladder reset / sample-layer flash on xCloud resolution changes** — the active rung stays put and resizes itself.
- Two pacing modes, wired to the existing "Low Latency Mode" toggle (now honest about what it does): **off = smooth** (one frame per refresh from a 2-frame queue; bursts become consecutive frames instead of drops), **on = present on arrival**.
- Thermal demotion: at `.serious`/`.critical` the coordinator drops to the sample floor and climbs back when the box cools.
- The fake `metal4fx` rung and the frame-interpolation rung are deleted (the LLFI file is gone). Ladder is now `metalfx → llsr → passthrough`, with a new **Preferred Upscaler** diagnostic (Auto / MetalFX / VideoToolbox SR) so you can A/B on the device without a rebuild.
- Sample-buffer floor rewritten on the tvOS 27 `AVSampleBufferVideoRenderer.Receiver` API: enqueue from the decode thread, host-clock timestamps via a render synchronizer, no `DisplayImmediately`. LLSR: two frames in flight, session started off the decode thread, per-frame forced telemetry removed, fallback flag actually honored.
- The app now requests a **60 Hz SDR display mode** (`AVDisplayCriteria`) when the first frame arrives — honoured if "Match Content" is on in tvOS settings.
- HUD shows a new `GPU` field (per-frame GPU time from command-buffer timestamps) — this is the number that tells you which scenario the A15 is in.

**Transport (fable-5.1 agent, reviewed by me)**
- Video transceiver pinned to H.264 via `setCodecPreferences` (640c first, then 42e0, then rtx/red/ulpfec/flexfec); VP8/AV1 no longer advertised. "VP9" removed from settings.
- Periodic keyframe timer off; keyframes are now requested on demand (rate-limited to one per 2 s) when the renderer reports decode trouble — and a decode failure no longer tears the session down.
- `audioJitterBufferFastAccelerate = true`, `audioJitterBufferMaxPackets = 50`; reconnect recreates the peer connection instead of dying on a closed one; `dataChannels` race fixed; stats parsing moved off the signaling thread with the missing video fields added (jitter buffer delay/target, `framesDropped`, freezes, `keyFramesDecoded`, decode time, nack/pli).

**Defaults / posture**
- Deployment target → tvOS 27 everywhere; dead `#available(tvOS 18/26)` checks removed.
- Defaults: Low Latency Mode **off**, Audio Boost **0 dB**, audio resync watchdog **off** (a one-time migration re-baselines existing installs for the two settings whose meaning changed).

## Verification (all on this machine, Xcode 27.0 / tvOS 27 SDK)
- App builds clean for the **simulator** and for the **device SDK** (the one that compiles the MetalFX code — the simulator SDK has no MetalFX): 0 errors, 0 new warnings.
- Tests: VideoRenderingKit 21/21, NorthstarCore 382/382, NorthstarModels 18/18, app `NorthstarTests` 151/151, StreamingCore 44/45 — the one failure is `InputChannelTests.slowSend_keepsPollingAndCoalescesFreshState`, a timing-based test in a file neither of us touched; it flaked for the transport agent too.

## What I could not verify here, in order of importance
1. **Real stream behaviour on the Apple TV.** The simulator can't run an xCloud session, has no MetalFX, and has no VideoToolbox LLSR. Everything above is compile- and unit-verified; the actual smoothness claim needs one session on your box with the HUD on, watching `GPU`, `Video Drops` and `Render Delay`.
2. The `Receiver` API is marked beta in the 27 SDK docs.
3. Whether the direct-to-drawable MetalFX path is accepted on the A15's driver (if not, the code logs once and uses the intermediate copy automatically).

Deferred, deliberately (need device validation and could break the server contract): unordered/unreliable input data channel, moving the `GCController` handler off the main queue.

parts.text:
Done — all three steps completed and verified.

**Committed** on `perf/render-pipeline-tvos27` (two commits on top of your `154d0b0`):
- `b380a99` — Pin the offer to H.264, stop the periodic keyframe timer, and bound the audio jitter buffer (the transport slice)
- `091fcae` — Move video presentation to a paced render thread and rebuild the upscale ladder for tvOS 27 (render pipeline, ladder, settings, deployment target, docs)

**Pushed** to `origin/perf/render-pipeline-tvos27` — GitHub offered a PR link: https://github.com/example-user/northstar/pull/new/perf/render-pipeline-tvos27. I did not merge into `main`.

**Deployed** to "Example Room" (Apple TV 4K 3rd gen, tvOS 27.0 build 24J5358a): signed Debug build with your development certificate (team 35FACKB24L), installed via `devicectl`, launched with `--terminate-existing`, and confirmed the `Northstar` process is alive on the box (pid 2761) a few seconds after launch.

When you start a stream, this is what to look at, in order:

1. **Settings → Playback → Stream Session**: leave *Upscaling* on and *Low Latency Mode* off for the first run (that's the smooth-paced default).
2. Turn on the stats HUD and read the diagnostics row: **`GPU`** is the per-frame MetalFX cost on the A15 — under ~10 ms means MetalFX is comfortably in budget; **`Video Drops`** should stay near zero on a decent connection; **`Status`** should read `metalfx` (or `passthrough` for the first second or so while the scaler compiles off-thread).
3. If `GPU` is high or the picture still stutters, flip **Settings → Diagnostics → Preferred Upscaler** to *VideoToolbox SR* — that's the on-device A/B I couldn't run from here. If it says `thermal-floor` after a long session, the box got hot and the coordinator deliberately dropped to the floor.
4. Toggle *Low Latency Mode* on if you'd rather have ~8 ms less input lag than perfectly even cadence.

If anything misbehaves, the console lines to look for are `[MetalRenderer]` (scaler build time, direct-drawable output) and `[StreamView] Render ladder …` (which rung was chosen and why).

## Goal
- Make Northstar (tvOS xCloud client, /Users/dev/code/northstar) deliver "buttery smooth gameplay": render-pipeline/ladder rewrite + transport fixes on tvOS 27; now: commit, push, and deploy the branch to the user's Apple TV.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User: "make sure you use fable 5.1 for all the audits, this needs genuine intelligence" → all agents were `anthropic/claude-fable-5-1`, reasoning_effort high.
- User: "remeber, we're anyway using tvos 27 for this" → tvOS 27 is the deployment floor; no tvOS 26 compat.
- User: cite Apple/primary sources; pushes back on unsupported estimates.
- User: "okay now go ahead and implement everything. i want a buttery smooth gameplay experience".
- User (latest, verbatim): "commit push and deploy to my tv".
- Repo rules (AGENTS.md): no new files without justification, keep `#if WEBRTC_AVAILABLE` guards, `@unchecked Sendable` only with documented invariant, Swift 6.2 strict concurrency, Swift Testing for new pure-Swift tests.
- Xcode.app is RUNNING — never kill/restart it; use headless `xcodebuild` with separate DerivedData (`/tmp/northstar-dd` sim, `/tmp/northstar-dd-device` device, `/tmp/northstar-dd-transport` was the agent's).

I'm working through which renderer during warming produces the sample-buffer view's last visible frame, since the Metal renderer is the only one attached to the track while the sample-buffer view stays hidden until the candidate is ready.

The log confirms the sample-buffer renderer received the first WebRTC frame at 420v format, then the switch to metalfx attempted, attaching Metal and detaching the sample renderer — but if Metal never calls back with candidate ready or failed, we're stuck in warming indefinitely with a frozen black frame. This matches the reported symptom of both input and output showing 1920x1080, which lines up with the sample renderer's snapshot being the baseline before the switch rather than the fallback target resolution.

So the real question becomes why the Metal renderer never signals readiness. It could be that the CAMetalDisplayLink never fires because the render thread's run loop isn't actually spinning, or because the display link requires the layer to be visible on screen and it isn't yet at the point the scaler is installed — either way, frames queue up but never get presented, so there's no success or failure signal to trigger the fallback.

Not visible or offscreen — that could mean CAMetalDisplayLink lacks a display association and never gets vsync callbacks. It's also possible the layer's frame is zero if the view was added without proper constraints, meaning drawableSize would be zero and no drawables get produced, which would explain a silent callback failure. I'm also considering whether the MetalFX scaler's resource preparation is happening at the wrong point in this sequence.

This creates a chicken-and-egg deadlock: the layer stays hidden until ready, but readiness requires a presented frame, and presenting requires a display link that only fires when visible. The older MTKView design avoided this because CADisplayLink is tied to the screen rather than the layer, so it kept firing even while the view was hidden, and `draw()` was called explicitly regardless. That's a meaningful behavioral difference introduced by switching to CAMetalDisplayLink.

Rather than keep speculating, I should verify by checking `MetalVideoRenderer.swift` to see exactly where `onCandidateReady` fires, how the display link gets created and attached, and what happens when the layer is hidden or zero-sized. Enabling verbose logs on-device would also help confirm this, though toggling that setting remotely isn't straightforward — I could try relaunching the app with a UserDefaults override via devicectl to force verbose logging on.

Found it: the ladder is stuck in "metalfx-warming" — the coordinator detaches the sample-buffer renderer and attaches a hidden Metal renderer that waits for its first presented frame, but that frame never arrives, leaving a black screen with the HUD frozen.
